edits.headline: NHS trust says 20 women had breasts removed unnecessarily
edits.subheadline: County Durham and Darlington NHS Foundation Trust found that more than 300 breast cancer patients suffered harm, the BBC reported.
editorialBody: County Durham and Darlington NHS Foundation Trust said 20 women had mastectomies they did not need, the Irish News reported on 18 September.
Of 539 cases reviewed by 2 September, 242 involved minor harm, 59 moderate harm and 19 severe harm, and one patient died. The review covers breast cancer cases from January 2023 to February 2025.
Chief executive Steve Russell said: "We are deeply sorry to the women and families who have been harmed and let down by failings in our breast services."
Russians began voting in a wartime parliamentary election set to secure the Kremlin's power, AFP reported on 18 September. Voting runs until 20 September, TASS reported.
A rout in Turkish investment funds erased $4bn from a rapidly won fortune, Bloomberg reported. A crisis at the Pusula and Tera funds led to market panic, according to Bloomberg.
Bitcoin recovered toward $78,000 on 18 September and the HYPE token led a rally in other cryptocurrencies, CoinDesk reported.
Scientists have discovered a new cat species in Bolivia, DW News reported.
